links.comparator_used: RAG without an authorization gate (single-pass retrieval and generation, unchecked)
links.outcome: Unjustified inference rate, appropriate refusal rate, and factual correctness
links.effect: EGDA unjustified inference 8.0% vs 47.7% for RAG; appropriate refusal 95.0% vs 56.9%; factual correctness 96.4% vs 74.5%
links.quote: In a controlled experiment using 60 breast cancer decision-snapshot cases (1,260 system outputs across three arms evaluated by LLM-as-Judge with expert calibration), EGDA reduced the unjustified inference rate to 8.0% (vs. 48.7% for unconstrained LLM and 47.7% for RAG; risk difference vs. unconstrained −40.7%, 95% CI −46.9 to −34.0, p < 0.001), raised the appropriate refusal rate to 95.0% (vs. 56.9% and 56.9%; risk difference vs. unconstrained +38.1%, 95% CI +31.3 to +44.5, p < 0.001), and achieved the highest factual correctness at 96.4% (vs. 69.8% and 74.5%).

links.comparator_used: Unconstrained LLM relying on its own knowledge (no retrieval)
links.outcome: Unjustified inference rate and appropriate refusal rate
links.effect: Unjustified inference 47.7% (RAG) vs 48.7% (unconstrained), p=0.870; appropriate refusal 56.9% vs 56.9%, p=1.0; factual correctness 74.5% vs 69.8%
links.quote: An unexpected finding was that retrieval-augmented generation without an authorization gate failed to reduce unjustified inference relative to the unconstrained baseline (47.7% vs. 48.7%, p = 0.870) and produced no improvement in appropriate refusal (56.9% vs. 56.9%, p = 1.0), showing that information supply alone is not sufficient for inferential governance.
